Flooding Disrupts Kyrgyzstan Metals & Mining Operations; Kyrgyzaltyn OJSC Among Firms Impacted

Heavy flooding across central and eastern Kyrgyzstan has severely disrupted operations in the country’s Metals & Mining industry, with major sites and transport routes affected as of Thursday, according to company statements and market analysts.

Torrential rains began late Tuesday and continued into Thursday morning, causing the Naryn and Saryjaz rivers to overflow and inundate key mining regions. The flooding has triggered mudslides and damaged access roads to several gold and rare earth extraction sites, forcing production halts and evacuation of non-essential staff.

Kyrgyzaltyn OJSC, the state-owned gold mining enterprise, confirmed in a statement that operations at its Kumtor processing plant have been “temporarily suspended” due to flooded access roads and power interruptions. “Our priority is the safety of our employees and protection of critical infrastructure,” the statement read. The company said it is coordinating with emergency services to assess damage and restore operations “as soon as conditions allow.”

A spokesperson for Central Metals Mining, another operator in the region, said that “significant logistical delays” are expected after a section of the main transport route to their Issyk-Kul mine was washed out by floodwaters. “We are evaluating alternate routes, but we anticipate at least a 60% reduction in output for the coming days,” the spokesperson said.

Preliminary estimates from the Kyrgyz Mining Association indicate that up to 40% of the country’s gold and rare earth mining output could be offline if flood conditions persist through the week. “This is the worst flooding we have seen in the past decade,” said association president Almazbek Sharipov. “If rains continue, the impact on output and exports could be substantial.”

Portions of the country’s rail infrastructure, crucial for transporting processed metals to border crossings with China and Kazakhstan, have also been affected. Rail operator representatives report delays of up to 48 hours, with further disruptions possible if water levels continue to rise.

Industry analysts warn that the flooding may lead to upward pressure on regional gold prices if production remains constrained. “Investors are watching closely,” said Elena Bakirova, a Bishkek-based metals analyst. “Extended outages at sites like Kyrgyzaltyn’s could tighten supply and cause volatility.”

With weather forecasts predicting continued rainfall over the next 48 hours, Metals & Mining firms in Kyrgyzstan are bracing for further disruptions and assessing the potential for long-term infrastructural damage. Emergency crews remain on site as companies work to protect assets and restore operations.
